# **Loyalty, Leveled Up: How We’re Building the Next Generation of Rewards**


[Global Technology](https://medium.com/@global_technology?source=post_page---byline--bde6eb70e682-----------------------------------------)


5 min read


·


Just now

*From simpler experiences to smarter systems, this is how loyalty evolves at global scale.*


Press enter or click to view image in full size


*by Sara Robertson, Sr. Manager, Product Management*


**Quick Bytes**


- Loyalty operates at massive scale, but customer research showed that finding, understanding, and using rewards didn’t always feel easy in the moments that mattered most
- By rethinking loyalty as a platform — not just a rewards list — teams reduced friction, introduced scalable personalization, and embedded value directly into the ordering journey
- The result is a simpler, more intuitive loyalty experience designed to grow with customers and support long-term global scale


Loyalty at McDonald’s operates at a scale few brands have ever achieved. Every day, millions of customers engage with McDonald’s Rewards — each with their own habits, preferences, and expectations. As the program grows, so does our ambition: **deliver a loyalty experience that feels effortless, personal, and genuinely valuable for everyone.**


That ambition is tied to a clear leadership focus: continuing to grow our global loyalty customer base by making loyalty so intuitive, flexible, and valuable that it becomes a natural part of how customers use the app. As McDonald’s continues its journey to build one of the world’s leading loyalty programs, simplicity and customer value remain at the center of every decision.


That’s why teams across Product, Engineering, and Experience Design — together with cross-functional partners across the Global team, segments, and markets — collaborated to reimagine the loyalty experience. As of September 2026, the experience is now live across all of our lead Global Mobile App (GMA) markets.


**Designing for growth starts with reducing friction**
Customer research made one thing clear early on: loyalty was valuable, but engaging with it didn’t always feel easy. Customers told us rewards could be hard to find, confusing to understand, or disconnected from the actual moment they were ordering food. Too often, rewards were remembered only after checkout — when it was already too late.


If loyalty is going to scale to hundreds of millions of active users, it has to work just as well for casual customers as it does for superfans. That means removing friction, reducing cognitive load, and making loyalty feel obvious at a glance.


The Experience Design team led discovery and validation across multiple markets, shaping the work around four guiding principles:


- Make rewards easier to access
- Surface value at the right moment
- Clarify how customers move between rewards and offers
- Introduce personalization in a way that can scale globally


**What’s live now: A simpler, clearer rewards experience**
The refreshed experience begins by making loyalty easier to understand the moment customers open the app. A dedicated **Rewards dashboard** provides a clear home for points and available rewards, removing the ambiguity of mixed content and giving loyalty its own clear space.


Press enter or click to view image in full size


From there, the rewards themselves are easier to browse and compare. Visual improvements and contextual cues help customers quickly understand what’s available to them right now — without guessing, scrolling endlessly, or running into dead ends. Rewards that can’t be redeemed have clear badges and visual cues to show why they’re unavailable, which reduces frustration and builds trust.


And because loyalty value doesn’t live in a vacuum, we also made it faster to find the right offers when you’re ready to order. Deals can now be filtered by fulfillment (like pickup versus delivery), so customers see what applies to their moment — less scrolling, fewer dead ends, and a quicker path from “that looks good” to “add to order.”


Though these changes may feel subtle, their impact is foundational: they lower the barrier to participation, making it easier for more customers to engage with loyalty consistently — an essential step toward growing active usage. We designed the experience to scale with our markets’ evolving needs, creating a strong foundation for future improvements.


**Curated rewards: Personalization becomes a reality**
One of the most important shifts in the new loyalty experience is the introduction of **Curated Rewards** — and this is where next‑generation loyalty truly begins.


Press enter or click to view image in full size


For the first time, loyalty moves beyond a static rewards list to an experience shaped by individual behaviors and preferences. Curated Rewards surface options based on a customer’s activity and purchase behavior. In testing, customers described the experience as feeling “chosen for me,” which reinforced confidence in the program and increased intent to redeem. User testing also showed that displaying the customer’s first name in the Rewards dashboard helped create a more personalized experience.


Behind the scenes, Curated Rewards are powered by a **Personalized Reward Store microservice** , introducing a dedicated service layer capable of delivering customer‑specific reward options. While the first use case focuses on food rewards, the significance goes far beyond the initial experience.


This capability creates a foundation for increasingly sophisticated customer experiences over time, supporting new reward types, partnerships, and future machine learning-driven innovations. In other words, Curated Rewards aren’t just a feature; they’re the start of a loyalty system designed to grow with customers as the program scales toward its long‑term goal.


**More ways to redeem** Another major milestone in that journey arrived in May with the launch of Points for Dollars Off in the U.S. Instead of redeeming points only through predefined reward options, eligible customers can now exchange points for dollars off their purchase, giving them greater flexibility in how they unlock value from the program.


Press enter or click to view image in full size


The launch instantly expanded redemption possibilities for millions of Rewards members and marked a meaningful shift in how loyalty is delivered. By introducing more choice into the redemption experience, we’re helping customers engage with rewards in a way that feels more relevant to their individual needs and ordering habits.


For the teams behind the experience, this new feature demonstrates how modern loyalty platforms can move beyond fixed reward structures to create more flexible, customer-centric experiences at scale. The capabilities built for Points for Dollars Off also establish a foundation for future innovations, allowing the loyalty experience to continue evolving alongside customer expectations.


**Building the next generation of loyalty**
Every one of these changes — simplifying the experience, introducing personalization, expanding redemption options, and embedding loyalty into natural customer moments — serves a shared purpose: **making loyalty easier to engage with for more people, more often** .


That’s how McDonald’s is evolving loyalty — not through a single feature, but through a loyalty platform designed to scale, adapt, and grow alongside its customers.


What’s live today is just the beginning. The next generation of loyalty is already taking shape.
